situation:
You and your teammate are the communications manager and the customer experience manager at VOLTLOOP RENEWED, a regional electronics recycler that collects, refurbishes and resells used phones, laptops and tablets. The vice president of retail operations (judge) oversees both of your functions and has asked the two of you to settle a question before the company opens its first stores outside its home state.

VOLTLOOP RENEWED has built its reputation over close to fifteen years on a simple promise: every refurbished device carries a ninety-day warranty. That warranty has always excluded battery capacity, because a used battery cannot be restored to factory condition. Customers in the home market have learned this over time, largely from store associates who explain it at the counter rather than from anything the company prints.

The new state's consumer statutes permit the exclusion to live in the written terms customers accept at checkout, provided those terms are available to read. Legal counsel has confirmed the current practice complies. Marketing research from the new market, however, shows shoppers there compare refurbished sellers on battery life first, and several competitors advertise a battery guarantee VOLTLOOP RENEWED does not intend to match.

One approach keeps the exclusion where it sits now, in the accepted terms, and trains associates to raise it when asked; checkout stays quick, but customers who discover the limit only when a battery fades will feel the company hid it. The other prints the exclusion on the price tag and requires associates to state it aloud before every sale, which costs sales to competitors and adds time to each transaction.

Grand-opening week and the trade-in surge that follows every new phone release will put long lines at the counters, and whatever the team decides has to survive those peaks without collapsing into a rushed sentence nobody hears. The vice president (judge) wants a recommendation on where the warranty's limits belong, the wording of a written notice for customers, and the spoken direction associates will be given at the counter.

You will present your recommendation to the vice president of retail operations (judge) in the vice president's office. The vice president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the vice president's questions, the vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of retail operations (judge) at VOLTLOOP RENEWED. Business background is the same as the situation above. The communications manager and the customer experience manager are coming to your office to recommend where the ninety-day warranty's battery exclusion belongs in the terms as the company opens its first out-of-state stores, to propose the wording of a written notice for customers, and to give you the spoken direction associates will follow at a busy counter.

You will greet the participant team and ask to hear their ideas. After they have presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: After this has been in place for a season, what would tell us it is working?
If associates start skipping the explanation when the line is long, what should we do about it?
